statement: For the curve $y=x^{3}-3x^{2}+2$, (i) find $\frac{dy}{dx}$ and the coordinates of the stationary points; (ii) determine their nature; (iii) find the equation of the tangent at $x=1$; (iv) deduce the interval on which the curve is decreasing and show that the value at the maximum exceeds that at the minimum by $4$.
solution: (i) $\frac{dy}{dx}=3x^{2}-6x=3x(x-2)$, zero at $x=0$ (where $y=2$) and $x=2$ (where $y=-2$). Stationary points $(0,2)$ and $(2,-2)$. (ii) $\frac{d^{2}y}{dx^{2}}=6x-6$. At $x=0$: $-6<0$ so maximum; at $x=2$: $6>0$ so minimum. (iii) At $x=1$, $y=0$ and slope $3-6=-3$. Tangent: $y=-3(x-1)$, i.e. $y=-3x+3$. (iv) The curve is decreasing where $\frac{dy}{dx}=3x(x-2)<0$, i.e. $0<x<2$. The maximum value is $2$ and the minimum is $-2$, and $2-(-2)=4$.
hints: Use the second derivative to classify.
